raw_response:
I will do mostly what has worked for me before, then push a little where I think the crop can pay me back. I have only 10.2 mu and just 2 people at home, so I cannot spread money everywhere. I will keep the wheat-maize land steady, because that is the backbone. On that land, I will put 7 mu into winter wheat, then the same 7 mu into summer maize after wheat harvest. The other 3.2 mu I will keep for stevia, because if I manage it well, it brings cash, but it also needs more watching. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a few yuan on fertilizer and lose grain, that hurts more than wasting a little. So I will feed wheat and maize a bit on the safe side, close to what the better fields around me use. Wheat I will water 3 times with my well if the season is normal: once after sowing if the ground is dry, once at jointing, once at filling. Maize I will water 2 times, one around big bell mouth and one when it is filling if rain is short. Stevia I will water more often because it does not like to sit dry for too long. I will use hybrid maize seed, improved wheat seed, and improved stevia seedlings if I can get a good batch. I will keep the wheat and maize fields fairly clean with 2 pesticide rounds each, and I will spray stevia more often because once insects and leaf disease get hold, the leaf quality drops. I will not chase fancy methods. I will do what I know, watch the weather, and if the crop looks weak, I will topdress rather than sit and regret it later.
